attempts.summary: Built a 3-node MariaDB Galera cluster on node1-node3 (CentOS Stream 10, mariadb-server 10.11.18 + mariadb-server-galera), loaded application data (appdb.orders), then added node4 as a fourth member via SST (mariabackup), verified it carries the existing data and accepts writes that replicate to all peers. Along the way fixed two environment issues: wrong wsrep_provider path (galera-4 -> galera) and an SELinux AVC denial blocking mariadb-backup's connectto to its own mysqld_t socket, resolved with a minimal custom SELinux module (mariabackup_sst) installed on all 4 nodes. Firewall ports 3306/4567(tcp+udp)/4568/4444 opened via firewalld on all nodes; mariadb enabled at boot on all 4. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1, node2, node3, then node4: captured boot_id baseline, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and confirmed each node auto-rejoined with wsrep_cluster_size=4, state Synced, status Primary, and appdb.orders intact (4 rows) before moving to the next node. Final cross-node check shows all 4 nodes consistent.
